newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Paper, Jujo Paper Board to merge on Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: Japan Paper, Jujo Paper Board to merge on Oct 1.

text.p: Japan Paper Industry Co Ltd and Jujo Paper Board Co Ltd said on Wednesday that they would merge on October 1, 1997.
The two companies are members of the Nippon Paper Industries Co Ltd group.
Four Japan Paper shares will be exchanged for one Jujo share, the two companies said in a statement. Japan Paper's face value is 50 yen and Jujo's face value is 500 yen, they said.
Japan Paper is the leading paper board maker in Japan. Jujo is unlisted.
The two companies expect the merged company to have a parent current profit of 1.57 billion yen and a net profit of 690 million yen on sales of 48.30 billion yen in the six months to March 31, 1998.
They expect the new company to have a parent current profit of 3.81 billion yen and a net profit of 1.75 billion yen on sales of 98.28 billion yen in the year to March 31, 1999.

Japan Paper posted a parent current profit of 2.13 billion yen and a net profit of 1.45 billion yen on sales of 52.77 billion yen in the year to December 31, 1995. Jujo posted a current profit of 2.14 billion yen and a net profit of 2.13 billion yen on sales of 40.59 billion yen in the year to March 31, 1996.
The name of the merged company will be decided by October 1, the two companies said. Jujo will be dissolved as a result of the merger, they said.
Japan Paper president Toru Imawaka will become president of the new company, they said.
The merged company will aim to expand its business and improve profitability as one of the major members of the Nippon Paper group, they said.
